title: US STOCKS-Wall St surges on upbeat earnings, hopes of end to govt. shutdown By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. US STOCKS-Wall St surges on upbeat earnings, hopes of end to govt. shutdown (For a live blog on the U.S. stock market, click LIVE/ or type LIVE/ in a news window.)
* Starbucks, Western Digital rise after results
* Senate in search for ways to end government shutdown
* Ten of the 11 major S&P sectors rise
* Intel drops as China slowdown hits earnings, forecast
* Indexes up: Dow 0.96 pct, S&P 0.98 pct, Nasdaq 1.23 pct
(Updates prices, adds comments, background)
By Shreyashi Sanyal
Jan 25 (Reuters) - U.S. stocks surged on Friday, as upbeat earnings reports helped investors put aside growth worries, with hopes of a resolution to the lengthy U.S. government shutdown fueling optimism.
With fourth-quarter earnings largely exceeding Wall Street expectations, the S&P 500 index .SPX was set to end a bumpy week, marked by concerns about slowing global growth and the government shutdown, on a high note.
The U.S. Senate was searching for a way to end a shutdown entering its 35th day and threatening the economy. signals an openness and willingness to compromise," said Oliver Pursche, chief market strategist of Bruderman Asset Management in New York. "It signals that we could see an open government as soon as Monday."
Ten of the 11 major S&P sectors were higher, with technology .SPLRCT and consumer discretionary .SPLRCD stocks providing the biggest boost.
Western Digital Corp WDC.O , whose quarterly results fell short of estimates, rose 5.13 percent after the hard-disk drive maker said its revenue would improve in the second half of the year. Shares of rival Seagate Technology STX.O climbed 5.66 percent. Corp INTC.O fell 6.5 percent after forecasting a dismal current quarter, blaming it on a slowdown in China and sluggish demand for its data center and modem chips. also capped further gains in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index .SOX which climbed 1.35 percent, after a near 6 percent surge on Thursday.
"Earnings are a mixed bag. But everyone had thought that this was so much more severe than it is. They are starting to realize that it's a slowdown, not a train going off the rails," said Arian Vojdani, investment strategist at MV Financial in Bethesda, Maryland.
Investors are bracing for an event-packed week ahead, which includes the Federal Reserve's first policy meeting this year, U.S. jobs data, another round of trade talks and reports from Apple Inc AAPL.O and Amazon.com Inc AMZN.O .
The Fed has forecast two more interest rate hikes in 2019, but Chairman Jerome Powell has stressed the central bank can be patient in approving any further hikes as officials gauge whether the U.S. economy will slow this year.
At 11:47 a.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was up 235.23 points, or 0.96 percent, at 24,788.47, the S&P 500 .SPX was up 25.80 points, or 0.98 percent, at 2,668.13 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was up 86.93 points, or 1.23 percent, at 7,160.39.
The consumer discretionary sector .SPLRCD rose 1.22 percent, led by 3.6 percent gain in Starbucks Corp SBUX.O after its quarterly sales topped estimates. a few weak spots were shares of AbbVie Inc (NYSE: ABBV ) ABBV.N which fell 6.30 percent after its quarterly profit missed estimates. the 112 companies in the S&P 500 companies that have reported quarterly results so far, 72.3 percent have surpassed profit expectations, according to Refinitiv data.
However, earnings growth estimates for the quarter have dropped to 14.3 percent from 20.1 percent at the start of October.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 4.63-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.86-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 11 new 52-week highs and no new lows, while the Nasdaq recorded 24 new highs and 10 new lows.
